newsitem.title: USA: Genetics Institute drug set for panel.
newsitem.headline: Genetics Institute drug set for panel.

text.p: Genetics Institute Inc said on Wednesday that its BeneFix recombinant Factor IX drug has been scheduled for review by a U.S. Food and Drug Administration advisory panel next month.

The company said the Blood Products Advisory Committee would review its application for marketing clearance of the hemophilia treatment on December 12. The independent advisory committees typically make recommendations to the FDA on whether to approve a drug.
In September Genetics Institute filed the drug, which is for treating Hemophilia B, with the FDA and with regulators in Canada and Europe.
Hemophilia B is caused by a deficiency or defect in Factor IX, one of several proteins involved in blood clotting.
American Home Products Corp holds a majority interest in Genetics Institute.
